name: Munter hitch
description: A friction hitch on a pear-shaped carabiner, for belaying or lowering without a belay device.
about:
In rescue it's mostly a backup: a belay or a light lower when a device is missing or has been dropped. It needs only the rope and a pear-shaped (HMS) locking carabiner, since a narrow carabiner pinches the hitch and stops it running smoothly.

Friction is greatest with the brake strand held alongside the load strand, and drops as the brake hand moves away from it. When the rope changes direction, from paying out to taking in, the hitch flips through the carabiner to its other side and works the same way, so there's no need to retie it.

Keep the brake strand on the spine side, away from the gate, where its rubbing could open the gate. The hitch twists the rope as it runs, and the rope rubbing on itself wears the sheath, so expect kinks to work out afterwards.

To hold the load hands-free, it's tied off with a mule knot backed up by an overhand, which can be released while the rope is loaded.
